items.headline: Dense Fog Advisory issued August 18 at 2:30AM AKDT until August 18 at 9:00AM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Visibility down to a quarter mile or less in dense fog.

* WHERE...Western Kupreanof Island and Kuiu Island.

* WHEN...Until 9 AM AKDT this morning.

* IMPACTS...Low visibility could make travel conditions hazardous.
items.instruction:
If driving, slow down, use your headlights, and leave plenty of
distance ahead of you.

items.description:

items.headline: Flood Watch issued August 17 at 12:35PM AKDT until August 18 at 4:00PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Including the following areas, Central Susitna Valley,
Southern Susitna Valley and Western Susitna Valley. This includes
the cities of Skwentna, Willow, Talkeetna, Trapper Creek, And
Petersville.

* WHEN...Through Tuesday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

items.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued August 17 at 12:01PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
ESFAFG

...Locations Impacted...
Upper Koyukuk Valley-Central Interior-South Slopes Of The Central
Brooks Range-Lower Koyukuk Valley-Middle Yukon Valley

Areas of up to 2 inches of rainfall are expected from the ongoing
event which may cause significant rises in the smaller headwater
streams that feed the Koyukuk and Middle Yukon Rivers.  As mainstem
rivers are currently low, there are no concerns for the larger rivers
in the area.

Rainfall rates are expected to decrease by Tuesday afternoon.
